olivia: Heads-up: Canary rollout of mixed INT8/FP8 kernels for redwood-13b is producing NaNs/Infs during long-context runs (~600 tokens+) in stage. Repro script below.

sam: Yikes. Any stack traces or kernel names?

olivia: Quick paste from stdout:
```
WARNING: numeric overflow detected in matmul: Inf produced
Traceback (most recent calls): ... runtime/kernel/gemm_int8_v2.cu:line 412: value=nan
kernel selected: gemm_int8_v2 (fallback: fp16_gemm)
also see fp8_rn_kernel for some layers
```

olivia: Repro command: `python tools/run_infer.py --model redwood-13b --precision mixed-int8-fp8 --context 2048 --input tests/long_prompt.txt --seed 42`

jing: Was this tested with the same calibration set used in perf bench? Calibration mismatch is the usual suspect. Did we use per-tensor scales or per-channel?

olivia: Calibration used last-week's small-sample JSON (~5k tokens) and per-tensor scales. I can re-run per-channel calibration but that will take longer.

rafael: Notes from profiling: when the KV cache grows, we see activation magnitudes drifting up in later layers -> softmax exponent values reach >1e3 and become Inf after quantization clipping. Profile snippet: `layer_22 attention exp max ~1.2e3` on failing runs vs `~3e1` on stable runs.

eva: That smells like accumulation/scale mismatch across caching. If FP8 exponent ranges don't match live activations, quantization saturates and then GEMM produces Infs. Two mitigation ideas: 1) apply activation clipping before softmax in attention, 2) use smoothquant to rebalance weights/activations.

sam: Also, LN (layernorm) in mixed precision has been brittle for us — small FP8 rounding can blow up variances. We used a small epsilon in fp16 builds; might need to increase epsilon for FP8 path.

olivia: Tried increasing layernorm eps from 1e-5 -> 1e-4 in canary, still hit infs but later.

rafael: Operational suggestion: pin kernel selection for canary to prefer fp16 for LayerNorm and softmax layers while keeping int8 for matmuls. We have `RW_KERNEL_OVERRIDE` env var — try `RW_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=prefer_fp16:layernorm,softmax`.

olivia: Will try that now. Also adding a post-infer NaN detector to fail-fast and route to fallback model variant.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment 2024-02-15T17:03 paused by olivia — reason: numeric instability detected :warning:

jing: For longer-term: incorporate smoothquant flow from the paper — per-channel alpha scaling (dividing weights by alpha, scaling activations by alpha) tends to reduce outliers and keeps scales smaller. We should try smoothquant calibration with our 50k-token diverse set.

sam: Agreed. Also test per-channel symmetric quantization for weights + asymmetric for activations; symmetric weights usually reduce extreme scale issues.

olivia: Quick experiment results (local):
```
baseline fp16: throughput 12 tok/s, p99 latency 230ms, no NaN
mixed-int8 fp8 (naive calib): throughput 22 tok/s, p99 190ms, NaN after ~600 tokens
mixed-int8 fp8 (per-channel calib + clipping 1e2): throughput 20 tok/s, p99 200ms, NaN reduced but seen at >1200 tokens
mixed-int8 fp8 (smoothquant + per-channel): throughput 19 tok/s, p99 205ms, no NaNs in 10k token test
```

rafael: Nice. Smoothquant seems promising despite small perf dip. We should capture that in kernel selection heuristics (prefer smoothquant kernels for long-context workloads).

eva: Add a KV cache health metric: monitor max activation exponent, fraction of clipped activations, and NaN rate. If any exceed thresholds, auto-fallback to fp16 for that request and increment a regression alarm.

sam: Also worth checking batching heuristics: large batch + long context increases effective sequence length per GPU and can push scales. Maybe reduce max_batch_size when avg_context > 1024.

olivia: Filed follow-ups:
- add smoothquant calibration job to perf pipeline (jira #INF-2321)
- implement NaN detector + auto-fallback (INF-2322)
- kernel override config for canaries and routing rules by workload shape (INF-2323)

jing: For calibration dataset, include adversarial long prompts (repeats, high dynamic range tokens) — we found that catches extreme activations earlier.

rafael: For now I'm rolling back the cluster-wide kernel selector to the previous stable profile and leaving the canary paused. We'll re-run after INF-2321/2322 land.

olivia: Thanks all. I'll attach more logs and a trimmed reproducer shortly. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary resume ready when infra flag `canary/mixed-quant` is toggled by olivia.
